_comment: Frozen claw data-tunnel wire vectors — the S0 byte-equality oracle.
Emitted from the live TunnelFrame encoder at 274f7cf5 (Product A P0 integrated
base), never hand-written. Every TunnelFrame variant is covered.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM THE CODE IT JUDGES: S0 moves the codec
into a neutral module. An oracle living inside the file under test would move
with it and could be regenerated by the very commit it is meant to judge. This
fixture lands in an EARLIER commit than the extraction, so its blob belongs to
a prior generation and 'the vectors were not regenerated' becomes a fact about
Claw behaviour must be byte-identical across the extraction. If a single wire
This is data, not a Cargo target: tests/data/*.json adds no test target, so
the R1a.7 inventory ratchet (199/149) is untouched.
encoding: hex of TunnelFrame::encode() — opcode byte followed by the body

vectors.name: health
vectors.note: FRAME_HEALTH 0x01; body is the claw-namespaced HEALTH_PROBE value

vectors.name: data
vectors.note: FRAME_DATA 0x11; raw bytes spanning the 0x7f/0x80 boundary

vectors.name: error
vectors.note: FRAME_ERROR 0x13; UTF-8 reason, no length prefix inside the frame

vectors.name: resize
vectors.note: FRAME_RESIZE 0x15; cols=120 rows=40 as two u16 big-endian

vectors.name: exit_code
vectors.note: FRAME_EXIT 0x16; discriminant 0x01 = Code, then i32 big-endian 0

vectors.name: exit_signal
vectors.note: FRAME_EXIT 0x16; discriminant 0x02 = Signal, then i32 big-endian 9

vectors.name: network_settings
vectors.note: FRAME_NETWORK_SETTINGS 0x17; canonical CBOR map, keys length-first: mtu(3), mesh_ipv4(9), session_id(10)
